lede: Tuesday is a full day at Town Hall — the newly seated Council takes up second reading of the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code, which would write new landscaping and historic-review standards into the Land Use Code, and the Telluride Housing Authority meets to hammer out a primary-residency policy for dependents in split-custody households, a gap that's tripped up real families. Wednesday the County Commissioners convene a special meeting with no agenda posted yet, and Thursday P&Z weighs in on three Town-owned development projects in the A2 zone, including the Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific.

notable.stake: Second reading vote on wildfire code changes to landscaping and historic review rules.
New policy on primary residency for split-custody dependents could affect deed-restricted households.
P&Z reviews subdivision and concept plans for Town-owned Carhenge and two other A2 projects.
Public hearing on KOTO's Live at the Drive liquor permit — residents may comment.
